html:
The Yangman are an Aboriginal people of the Northern Territory, in country south of Katherine around the upper Roper River and Mataranka.

Their neighbours were the Mangarrayi to the east, the Jawoyn to the north and the Mudburra to the south. In the 1880s cattle runs took over the Roper country. Elsey Station, on Yangman and Mangarrayi land, became famous through Jeannie Gunn's book We of the Never Never (1908), which describes the Aboriginal people of the station from a settler's point of view.

The Yangman language has very few speakers today. For the deeper past, see Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Yangman are an Aboriginal people of the Northern Territory, in country south of Katherine around the upper Roper River and Mataranka.
